slides.title: Why the US
K-beauty is the growth engine of US facial skincare: its sales nearly doubled to $3.6B in four years

claims.claim: K-beauty sales nearly doubled to $3.6B in four years
38.6% of the category's growth in 2021–25 came from K-beauty brands
K-beauty brands: share of US facial skincare rose from 9% to 15% in four years
Other brands: sales grew 15% over the period, against 89% for K-beauty
For Onsoo: the fastest-growing pool in the category already rewards Korean skincare brands
A 2026 trade-press figure of $5.2B for the "US K-beauty market" also counts makeup and hair care, so it is not comparable and is not used

slides.title: Amazon is the front door to US K-beauty, with 41% of sales and 61% of buyers shopping there most often

claims.claim: Amazon sells half again as much K-beauty skincare as specialty beauty stores
evidence: Share of 2025 K-beauty skincare sales: Amazon 41%; Specialty beauty retail 27%; Mass retail 14%; Brand websites (DTC) 12%; Other 6%

claims.claim: Buyers agree, and they find new brands on TikTok twice as often as in stores
evidence: Buy K-beauty on Amazon most often 61%; Buy at specialty beauty most often 22%; Found last new brand on TikTok 38%; Found last new brand in a store 17% (survey of 1,200 women aged 18–44, September 2026)

claims.claim: Price helps too: 52% of K-beauty triers cite it, and the cream is $24 on Amazon, $28 in stores

slides.title: Onsoo's Amazon pilot shows real pull, with units nearly doubling in six months, 4.5 stars and repeat near benchmark

claims.claim: Sales rose every month with only three SKUs listed by a cross-border seller
evidence: Units sold: Jan 7,400; Feb 8,600; Mar 10,100; Apr 11,800; May 12,900; Jun 14,000

claims.claim: Customers rate it well and come back at the rate of other new brands
evidence: 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews: Strong for a brand almost unknown in the US
29% buy again within 90 days: Close to the 31% first-year Amazon benchmark
Top complaint (6% of reviews): Korean-only labels, fixed by US labels
Onsoo's 48% in Korea shows the headroom

claims.claim: The plan's 300,000 units for 2027 are 1.8 times the June run-rate, from seven SKUs instead of three
evidence: Run-rate = June 2026 units × 12 = 168,000 units; Option A adds four SKUs from 2027 (planning team)

slides.title: Route economics
Retail keeps more per unit than Amazon, $7.54 against $4.72, but its fixed costs swallow the advantage

claims.claim: On Amazon, fees and ads take 61% of the price
evidence: Amazon per unit, ads at 25% ACoS: Price $24; Referral fee $3.6; FBA fee $5.1; Ads $6; Landed cost $4.575; Contribution $4.725

claims.claim: In stores, the retailer's half of the shelf price is the largest cost
evidence: Specialty retail per unit: Shelf price $28; Retailer margin $14; Co-op $1.12; Returns $0.56; Landed cost $4.775; Contribution $7.545

claims.claim: Covering retail's $7.5M of yearly fixed costs takes nearly a million units; the best plan year has 234,000

slides.title: On the planning team's own inputs, retail-led breaks the cash cap, while Amazon-led pays back by 2030

claims.claim: Retail-led breaks the cash cap, while Amazon-led pays back by 2030
evidence: 115.5% of the $18M cap used by retail-led at end-2030, with cash still falling

claims.claim: Amazon-led: the low point comes in the launch year; cash flow turns positive in 2028 and the total is above zero in 2030
Retail-led: cash flow is negative in every year, as $9.6M of fixed costs a year outrun contribution
Payback: only Amazon-led brings cumulative cash back to zero within four years of launch, as the board requires

slides.title: Retail's own costs sink the route: by 2030 it earns back less than a third of what it spends

claims.claim: 29.4% of the $31.6M retail spend in 2027–30 comes back as contribution
evidence: Effect on cumulative cash vs Amazon-led, $M: Retail contribution 5.29659; Amazon halo 3.98318; Extra inventory -0.8757; Launch fee, fixtures -1.6; Retail marketing, field sales -30

claims.claim: Retail marketing, field sales: $7.5M a year, the one cost that decides the case
Retail contribution: 600–1,000 doors at 4.5 units a week sell too few units to matter
Amazon halo: even taken at face value, the 1.3 times uplift recovers only a small part of the spend

slides.title: Retail-led would also pull group operating margin below the 8% floor in each of its first three years

claims.claim: Retail-led would pull group operating margin below the 8% floor in each of its first three years
evidence: Board floor 8.0%

claims.claim: The floor binds in the launch years, when retail costs peak
evidence: 2027: national marketing, field sales and launch costs make the US a $8.7M operating loss
2028–29: the US loss shrinks, but not fast enough to lift the group back to the floor

claims.claim: Amazon-led: stays above the floor in every year, because its US loss is small even at launch
Retail-led would need the board to waive the margin floor as well as the cash cap and the payback rule

slides.title: Retail-led inputs
The plan's 4.5 units per door a week needs a known brand; at Onsoo's awareness, newcomers would be delisted

claims.claim: The plan's 4.5 units per door a week needs a known brand
evidence: Median units per door per week by aided awareness: Below 10% (Onsoo) 2.6; 10–20% 3.5; Above 20% 4.6; Option B plan 4.5
Retailer removal line 4.0

claims.claim: Onsoo would be judged against the removal line after 12 months
evidence: Below 10% (Onsoo): aided awareness is 4% among category buyers and 9% among K-beauty buyers
Upper quartile: even 3.4 units, the top quarter of low-awareness newcomers, sits under the 4.0 line

claims.claim: Option B plan: matches the median of brands already above 20% awareness
Retail volume at the low-awareness median is 57.8% of plan
evidence: 2.6 ÷ 4.5 units per door a week
Sell-through: retail analytics firm, 46 newcomer brands, 2025

slides.title: Neither the halo nor peer history supports retail-first, and Amazon-first worked for one entrant in three

claims.claim: The 1.3 times halo rests on a correlation, not a cause
evidence: Across 30 K-beauty brands, doors and Amazon sales correlate at 0.71
Brands that sell well on Amazon win more doors, so the arrow can run either way
Only 17% of K-beauty buyers found their last new brand in a store, against 38% on TikTok

claims.claim: Saebom went Amazon-first and added stores once sales were proven
evidence: Entered the US on Amazon in 2022
Reached about $30M of US revenue by 2025
Added 300 specialty doors in 2025, three years after entry

claims.claim: Mooncrest went retail-first and lost more than our whole cash cap
evidence: Launched in 450 doors in 2023
Removed from shelves in 2025, after the retailer's review
Estimated cumulative US loss above the board's $18M cap
$21M Mooncrest estimated US loss

claims.claim: Amazon-first is no guarantee: two of three such entrants stayed small
evidence: Gaon Lab entered on Amazon in 2022
Yeoreum entered on Amazon in 2023
Both stayed below that US revenue in 2025, hence the guardrails in section 5
$5M US revenue ceiling, each, 2025

slides.title: With realistic sell-through and no halo, retail-led would lose about $26.4M by 2030

claims.claim: With realistic sell-through and no halo, retail-led would lose about $26.4M by 2030
evidence: −$20.8M retail-led on the planning team's inputs: 4.5 units per door a week and the 1.3 times halo
− $3.5M halo removed: Amazon sells the Option A volumes (contribution less the inventory it needs)
− $2.1M doors sell 2.6 units a week, the median for brands below 10% awareness
= −$26.4M cumulative cash at end-2030, against the $18M cap

claims.claim: The estimate changes only two of the plan's inputs, and it is still generous to retail
evidence: Specialty doors sell 2.6 units per door a week, the median for newcomers below 10% aided awareness (Table 8), instead of 4.5
Amazon sells the Option A volumes: the 1.3 times halo is dropped, because the correlation behind it does not show cause
Everything else as in the plan: 600–1,000 doors, $9.6M of fixed costs a year, 25% ACoS, four months of inventory

claims.claim: At 2.6 units a door, the retailer would remove Onsoo after 12 months, as it removed Mooncrest, whose loss was $21M

slides.title: Amazon-led risk
Ad cost is the swing factor: at the benchmark rate for scaling brands, Amazon-led ends 2030 $2.3M short of payback

claims.claim: Ad cost is the swing factor: at the benchmark rate, Amazon-led ends 2030 $2.3M short of payback
evidence: Cumulative cash end-2030, $M: Plan ACoS 25% 2.39975; Duty 25%, ACoS 25% 1.28792; Pilot ACoS 28% 0.37655; Benchmark ACoS 32% -2.32105; ACoS 32% and duty 25% -3.43288; Top of range ACoS 38% -6.36745
$2.4M plan − $0.7M lost per percentage point of ACoS × 7 pp = −$2.3M benchmark case
ACoS benchmark: agency data, median 32%, range 26%–38%. Cash per percentage point of ACoS = 2,810,000 units (2027–30) × $24 × 1%

claims.claim: Payback is at risk; the cash cap is not
evidence: Benchmark, 32%: the median for brands scaling from $5M to $20M on Amazon, the band Onsoo's plan crosses
Duty 25%: the tariff decision due in mid-2027 costs about $1.1M of cumulative cash by 2030
Top of range, 38%: even then the deficit is 35% of the $18M cap, so the downside is contained

slides.title: Amazon-led pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6% of Amazon sales

claims.claim: Amazon-led pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6% of Amazon sales
evidence: $10.7 contribution per unit before ads − $3.9 fixed, set-up and inventory costs per unit ($10.9M ÷ 2,810,000 units) ÷ $24 Amazon price = 28.6%

claims.claim: The line sits just above the pilot and well below the benchmark
evidence: Volumes as planned: 2,810,000 Amazon units over 2027–30 from seven SKUs
US fixed costs of $2.1M a year plus $0.8M of set-up in 2027; four months of landed cost held as inventory
Duty stays at 15%; at 25% the break-even falls to about 26.9%
The pilot ran at 28% on a small budget; the agency benchmark for brands at Onsoo's planned scale is 32%

claims.claim: Make ACoS the launch's lead indicator: review it every quarter and act before it reaches 28.6%

slides.title: Recommendation and plan
Amazon-led is the only US route inside the board's limits, and it builds nearly four times the revenue Japan would add

claims.claim: Amazon-led is the only US route inside the board's limits
evidence: Board limit: $40M revenue 2030; −$18M lowest cumulative cash; $0M cumulative cash end-2030; 8% lowest group margin
A · Amazon-led: $26.4M; −$1.9M; $2.4M; 9.5%; Recommended / Passes every limit; reaches two-thirds of the $40M ambition
B · Retail-led: $37.6M; −$20.8M; −$20.8M; 4.5%; Fails the cash cap, payback and margin floor

claims.claim: it builds nearly four times the revenue Japan would add
evidence: J · Japan scale-up: $7M; −$1.1M; $1.8M; 10.1%; Passes, but adds little in a market growing 1.5% a year

slides.title: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the limits; Amazon-led gets two-thirds of the way, and the ambition needs restating

claims.claim: 66% of the $40M ambition reached by Amazon-led in 2030
evidence: Ambition $40.0M

claims.claim: Amazon-led: grows every year on the plan's volumes, but 2030 lands well short of the ambition
Retail-led: comes closer only on optimistic inputs, and breaks the cash cap to get there
Restate the goal: about $26M by 2030, with $40M as a later target that a gated retail phase 2 must earn

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: We recommend Amazon-led entry in 2027, a restated ambition and gated retail. Approve Amazon-led US entry for 2027 and restate the ambition: about $26M by 2030, with $40M as a later target that a gated retail phase 2 must earn; add specialty retail only once Amazon sales pass $10M a year and aided awareness passes 20%.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended / Passes every limit; reaches two-thirds of the $40M ambition ($26.4M revenue in 2030, lowest cash −$1.9M, end-2030 cash $2.4M, lowest margin 9.5%). Pays back only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%.

Fails the cash cap, payback and margin floor (−$20.8M cumulative cash, 4.5% margin in 2027), even on planning-team inputs; on realistic sell-through and no halo would lose about $26.4M by 2030. Would need the board to waive the margin floor as well as the cash cap and payback rule.
Passes, but adds little in a market growing 1.5% a year ($7M revenue in 2030); bandwidth allows one major launch in 2027, Japan remains an option once the US launch is stable.
Gate moved from 15% to 20% awareness: at 10–20%, newcomers sell 3.5, under the 4.0 line.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Amazon-led pays back only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6%; at the 32% benchmark ACoS, cash ends 2030 at −$2.3M; at 38% the deficit is 35% of the $18M cap
Duty 25%: the tariff decision due in mid-2027 costs about $1.1M of cumulative cash by 2030; at 25% duty the ACoS break-even falls to about 26.9%
The 1.3 times halo rests on a correlation, not a cause
Amazon-first is no guarantee: two of three such entrants stayed small
The planning team applies the hero product's economics to all SKUs
Japan cash excludes working capital, which the pack does not give
Plan's 2027 volume of 300,000 units is 1.8 times the June run-rate, from seven SKUs instead of three
Synthetic benchmark data: the company and all figures are fictional

Hire the US team and launch the four new SKUs with off-Amazon social marketing — US general manager (to hire), H2 2027
Run a quarterly guardrail review: ACoS against 28.6%, repeat against 31%, awareness toward 20% — CFO and CMO, from launch
